articles.abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is the most prevalent chronic joint disorder in orthopedics, with its underlying pathogenic genes and effective treatment methods remaining unclear. Resveratrol (RES), a potent bioactive natural polyphenol, has been shown to effectively alleviate KOA; however, its complex regulatory mechanisms require further investigation. This research seeks to clarify the molecular mechanisms by which RES contributes to the treatment of KOA, utilizing a blend of bioinformatics approaches and experimental validation. First, gene expression profiles related to KOA were obtained from the GEO database. Subsequently, differential gene analysis was conducted on the samples, and modular genes linked to KOA were extracted through the application of a weighted gene co-expression network. The LASSO algorithm was utilized to identify crucial pathogenic genes in KOA, which were later confirmed using clinical samples. Targets for RES were sourced from traditional Chinese medicine databases, and the therapeutic targets for KOA treatment were determined by finding the intersection of these sources. An enrichment analysis was carried out based on the therapeutic targets identified. Molecular docking studies were conducted to further assess the binding affinity of key therapeutic genes with RES. Lastly, animal experiments were implemented to substantiate the molecular mechanisms by which RES acts in the treatment of KOA. We identified 460 module genes and 10 key predictive genes through LASSO analysis. The findings from the enrichment analysis concerning potential therapeutic targets for RES in the treatment of KOA reveal that the significant genes implicated include VEGFA, IL6, MAPK3, IL1B, CASP3, and AKT1. Subsequent validation with clinical samples revealed that IL6, MAPK3, IL1B, CASP3, and AKT1 were significantly elevated during the progression of KOA, while VEGFA was markedly reduced in the context of KOA. The outcomes of the GO and KEGG analyses suggest that the primary biological processes implicated encompass apoptosis, the FoxO signaling pathway, the IL-17 signaling pathway, cellular senescence, and the NF-κB signaling pathway. The findings from the immune infiltration analysis indicate that resting CD4 memory T cells, memory B cells, resting mast cells, eosinophils, and activated mast cells may have important functions in the immune mechanisms related to KOA. The results of animal experiments demonstrate that RES effectively inhibits the expression of inflammatory factors such as IL-6, MAPK3, IL-1β, CASP3, and AKT1 during the progression of KOA, promotes the expression of VEGFA, and concurrently suppresses the FoxO signaling pathway and the IL-17 signaling pathway, thereby reducing cartilage damage induced by MIA and delaying the progression of KOA. In summary, RES can regulate the expression of genes including VEGFA, IL-6, MAPK3, IL-1β, CASP3, and AKT1, inhibit the FoxO signaling pathway and the IL-17 signaling pathway, alleviate cartilage damage induced by MIA, and delay the progression of KOA.

articles.title: Phytochemical Profiling and Multi-Target Wound-Healing Potential of Millettia extensa (Benth.) Baker Stem Bark Extracts: Integrated Computational and Experimental Validation.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Millettia species (Fabaceae) are traditionally used across parts of Asia and Africa for managing wounds, skin infections, and inflammatory disorders. Millettia extensa (Benth.) Baker is traditionally associated with the management of wounds and inflammatory conditions. However, its stem bark has not been systematically evaluated for wound-healing activity. AIM OF THE STUDY: To investigate the wound-healing potential of methanol (MEM) and aqueous (MEA) extracts of M. extensa stem bark using integrated in-silico, in-vitro and in-vivo experimental approaches. MATERIALS AND METHODS: MEM and MEA were subjected to preliminary phytochemical screening, estimation of total phenolic and flavonoid contents, and UHPLC-ESI-QTOF-MS/MS profiling. The shortlisted phytoconstituents were subsequently analyzed using network pharmacology and molecular docking against AKT1, IL-1β, STAT3 and TNF-α, while isoliquiritigenin was further evaluated by 200-ns molecular dynamics simulation. The extracts were further evaluated for antioxidant activity using the DPPH assay, antimicrobial activity using agar well diffusion and broth microdilution assays, acute toxicity and wound-healing activity using the HaCaT scratch-wound assay, carrageenan-induced paw edema model, and excision and incision wound models. Extract-based ointments were evaluated in the topical wound-healing models. RESULTS: MEM contained higher phenolic (108.59 mg GAE/g) and flavonoid (71.84 mg QE/g) contents than MEA (49.28 mg GAE/g and 40.59 mg QE/g, respectively), with 28 and 63 tentatively annotated compounds, respectively. Network pharmacology identified 86 shared wound-healing targets, among which AKT1, TNF, STAT3, and IL-1β emerged as key hub targets. Isoliquiritigenin exhibited consistent multi-target docking affinities (-9.1 to -6.8 kcal/mol) and the isoliquiritigenin-AKT1 complex showed relatively stable conformational behaviour during the 200-ns molecular dynamics simulation. MEM showed stronger DPPH radical-scavenging activity (IC50 = 64.01 μg/mL) and greater antimicrobial activity, with a MIC of 1.56 mg/mL against P. aeruginosa, S. aureus, and S. epidermidis, compared with MEA. Both extracts showed no observable signs of acute toxicity under the tested conditions. Notably, the 10 % MEM ointment produced 99.2 ± 1.1% excision wound closure, 42.40 ± 1.83 μg/mg hydroxyproline content, and tensile strength comparable to the standard treatment. CONCLUSION: Collectively, the present findings indicate that Millettia extensa stem bark, particularly the methanol extract, has promising wound-healing potential, with the observed activity accompanied by antioxidant, antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, and wound-repair effects. The integrated experimental and computational findings provide a basis for further mechanistic studies and validation of its potential application in topical wound management.

articles.title: Yujin Powder alleviates colonic oxidative injury in mice with dampness-heat diarrhea through the Keap1/Nrf2/GSH pathway: baicalein as a candidate key constituent.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Yujin Powder (YJP), a classic traditional Chinese medicinal formula for dampness-heat diarrhea (DHD), is widely used to treat damp-heat diarrhea in animals such as cattle and horses. However, the precise mechanisms by which YJP exerts its antioxidant effects in the treatment of DHD via the Keap1/Nrf2/GSH signaling pathway have not been fully elucidated. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to investigate the mechanisms by which YJP ameliorates oxidative injury in the colonic epithelium of DHD mice and to identify candidate active constituents potentially involved in this process. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A DHD mouse model was established and treated with YJP. Therapeutic efficacy was assessed based on hematological parameters, serum biochemical indices, blood viscosity, colonic inflammatory responses, and histopathological changes. Transcriptomic analysis was performed to characterize gene expression alterations in the colon. Mechanistic validation was conducted using qRT-PCR, Western blotting, and multiplex immunofluorescence. Furthermore, an in vitro oxidative stress model using LPS-stimulated NCM-460 cells was established to verify the antioxidant activity of baicalein, a candidate key constituent of YJP identified through virtual screening and molecular dynamics simulations. RESULTS: YJP significantly alleviated diarrhea symptoms in DHD mice, improved body weight loss, corrected metabolic disorders, reduced systemic and colonic inflammatory responses, and restored colonic epithelial integrity. Mechanistic studies demonstrated that YJP enhanced antioxidant defense by regulating the Keap1/Nrf2/GSH pathway, thereby reducing oxidative stress and epithelial injury. Through virtual screening and molecular dynamics simulations, baicalein was identified as a candidate key constituent of YJP and showed the potential to form stable interactions with both Keap1 and Nrf2. In vitro experiments further confirmed that baicalein markedly attenuated LPS-induced oxidative stress in NCM-460 cells, supporting its role as an important contributor to the antioxidant effects of YJP. CONCLUSION: YJP alleviates colonic oxidative injury in DHD mice by regulating the Keap1/Nrf2/GSH pathway, while baicalein may represent a candidate key constituent contributing to this antioxidant effect.

articles.title: Ampelopsis grossedentata alleviates vascular cognitive impairment in BCAS mice by regulating VEGFA/KDR/FGFR1-mediated angiogenesis and GSK3β/Bcl-2/Bax-mediated mitochondrial apoptosis.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Ampelopsis grossedentata (Hand.-Mazz.) W.T. Wang (vine tea) is a time-honored ethnomedicine used by the Tujia and Miao minorities in Southern China. It has traditionally been used for "clearing heat and detoxifying", "activating blood and unblocking collaterals", and "subduing liver-yang to resolve phlegm and eliminate turbidity". Its aqueous infusion is consumed as a folk remedy to alleviate vertigo, dizziness, and hypertension-related cardio-cerebrovascular symptoms. These traditional applications suggest its potential therapeutic relevance to chronic cerebral hypoperfusion-induced vascular cognitive impairment. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to investigate the protective effects and underlying mechanisms of vine tea aqueous extract against chronic cerebral hypoperfusion-induced vascular cognitive impairment, focusing on its regulation of angiogenic signaling and mitochondrial apoptosis-related pathways. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The chemical profile of vine tea aqueous extract was characterized by UPLC-Q-TOF-MS, and selected constituents were quantified. Network pharmacology and bioinformatics analysis using the GSE122063 dataset were performed to identify active constituents and candidate therapeutic targets. Molecular docking and 200-ns molecular dynamics simulations evaluated their binding stability. Male C57BL/6 mice were randomly divided into five groups (n = 20/group): Sham, Model, positive control (nimodipine, 11.7 mg/kg), VTL (100 mg/kg), and VTH (200 mg/kg). Vascular cognitive impairment was induced by microcoil-induced bilateral common carotid artery stenosis (BCAS). After a 1-week recovery period, mice received daily oral gavage for 30 days. Behavioral performance was assessed using the open field test, novel object recognition test, and Morris water maze. Cerebral perfusion, CD31-positive microvascular density, myelin integrity, neuronal morphology, neuronal apoptosis, and mitochondrial ultrastructure were assessed. Biochemical assays determined oxidative stress, ATP and lactic acid levels, while related genes and proteins were examined by RT-PCR and Western blotting. RESULTS: UPLC-Q-TOF-MS identified 31 compounds, among which dihydromyricetin, quercetin, taxifolin, aromadendrin, catechin, epigallocatechin and naringenin (predicted OB ≥ 20%, DL ≥ 0.18) were quantitatively determined. Network analysis identified seven hub targets, including a pro-angiogenic module (VEGFA, KDR, FGFR1) and an apoptosis-related module (GSK3β, RAF1, BCL2, BAX). Molecular docking and dynamics simulations supported stable interactions between the major constituents and hub targets. In BCAS mice, vine tea significantly improved cognitive behavior, restored regional cerebral blood flow (P < 0.01) and increased CD31-positive microvascular density (P < 0.05), while preserving myelin integrity (P < 0.01) and hippocampal neuron survival (P < 0.05). These benefits were accompanied by attenuated mitochondrial ultrastructural damage, increased ATP, SOD, and GSH levels, and reduced lactate and MDA content (P < 0.05), as well as decreased cleaved caspase-3/NeuN double-positive apoptotic neurons (P < 0.05). Mechanistically, VT restored VEGFA/KDR/FGFR1 expression, increased Bcl-2/Bax ratio and GSK3β phosphorylation, and normalized RAF1 hyperphosphorylation, suggesting coordinated regulation of angiogenic signaling and mitochondrial apoptosis-related pathways. CONCLUSIONS: Vine tea ameliorated cognitive deficits and hippocampal neuronal injury in BCAS mice by restoring VEGFA/KDR/FGFR1-mediated angiogenic signaling and rebalancing GSK3β/RAF1 and Bcl-2/Bax-related mitochondrial apoptotic pathways. These findings suggest vine tea as a promising multi-target ethnomedicinal candidate for vascular cognitive impairment, although the causal link between these two processes warrants further mechanistic validation.

articles.title: Sequential Stage-Specific Administration of Bushen-Tiaojing Decoctions II and III Ameliorates Mitochondrial Dysfunction in Ovarian Granulosa Cells of COH Mice by Regulating GRP75-Mediated MAM Homeostasis.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) offers a distinct therapeutic approach to infertility. Bushen-Tiaojing Decoctions II (BSTJ-II-D) and III (BSTJ-III-D; collectively, BSTJD) are clinical formulas developed by Professor Huilan Du according to the TCM theory of stage-specific treatment and are widely used in the clinical management of infertility. Previous studies have shown that sequential, stage-specific administration of these formulas can improve mitochondrial energy metabolism and increase pregnancy rates among infertile women undergoing in vitro fertilization and embryo transfer (IVF-ET). However, whether this sequential treatment improves mitochondrial function in ovarian granulosa cells (GCs) by preserving mitochondria-associated endoplasmic reticulum membrane (MAM) homeostasis remains unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: Glucose-regulated protein 75 (GRP75) is a key tethering protein that maintains MAM homeostasis. This study aimed to determine whether sequential, stage-specific administration of BSTJ-II-D and BSTJ-III-D ameliorates mitochondrial dysfunction in ovarian GCs by regulating GRP75-mediated MAM homeostasis. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A controlled ovarian hyperstimulation (COH) mouse model was established, after which animals received BSTJ-II-D and BSTJ-III-D sequentially via oral gavage. A group treated with GRP75-IN-1, a novel small-molecule compound that targets and binds GRP75, was included as a control. MAM morphology, mitochondrial bioenergetic activity, and mitochondrial biogenesis were systematically evaluated. For the in vitro experiments, human KGN ovarian granulosa-like tumor cells were transduced with a GRP75-overexpressing lentiviral construct to clarify how elevated GRP75 expression affects MAM architecture and function and subsequently influences mitochondrial homeostasis. Protein levels of GRP75, voltage-dependent anion channel 1 (VDAC1), mitochondrial calcium uniporter (MCU), sirtuin 1 (SIRT1), peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor γ coactivator 1α (PGC-1α), and nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2) were assessed in GCs. Cellular adenosine triphosphate (ATP) production, reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, mitochondrial Ca2+ loading, and mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP) were determined using fluorescence-based assays. In addition, mitochondrial permeability transition pore (mPTP) opening was evaluated quantitatively by flow cytometric analysis. RESULTS: Sequential BSTJD treatment attenuated COH-induced aberrant GRP75 overexpression, restored MAM ultrastructural integrity, reduced mitochondrial oxidative stress (OS) and Ca2+ overload, and enhanced mitochondrial energy metabolism and biogenesis. Mechanistically, BSTJD increased the expression of SIRT1, PGC-1α, and Nrf2 while inhibiting activation of the PERK/ATF4 pathway, thereby alleviating endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress and enhancing mitochondrial energy metabolism and biogenesis. GRP75-IN-1 reproduced the protective effects of BSTJD. Conversely, GRP75 overexpression in KGN cells disrupted MAMs and impaired mitochondrial function, further supporting GRP75 as a key mediator of the protective effects of BSTJD. CONCLUSION: Sequential BSTJD treatment preserves MAM homeostasis by suppressing aberrant GRP75 overexpression, thereby mitigating OS and mitochondrial Ca2+ overload. It also activates the SIRT1-PGC-1α-Nrf2 pathway to restore mitochondrial energy metabolism and biogenesis, ultimately ameliorating mitochondrial dysfunction in GCs. These findings provide new molecular evidence supporting the Bushen Tiaojing therapeutic approach for infertility.

articles.title: Poly(hexamethylenebiguanide) hydrochloride induces craniofacial cartilage defects and alters Wnt signaling related gene expression in zebrafish larvae.
articles.abstract: Poly(hexamethylenebiguanide) hydrochloride (PHMB) is widely used as a broad spectrum antimicrobial preservative, but its effects on craniofacial cartilage development require further characterization. Here, zebrafish were used to evaluate the developmental effects of PHMB following embryonic exposure to 0.15, 0.35, or 0.55 mg/L from 6 to 72 hours post fertilization (hpf). PHMB exposed larvae exhibited craniofacial cartilage malformations alongside general developmental abnormalities and altered locomotor behavior. These phenotypic changes were accompanied by increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) associated fluorescence, reduced proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA) fluorescence intensity, and increased TUNEL positivity in the craniofacial region. qRT-PCR analysis of pooled larval heads revealed downregulation of cartilage development related genes and altered expression of inflammation related genes. Changes were also observed in the expression of Wnt signaling related genes, including β-catenin, lef1, and axin2. Furthermore, in separate rescue experiments, astaxanthin (AST) and the Wnt signaling agonist BML-284 each partially alleviated the craniofacial abnormalities. Taken together, these findings provide experimental evidence of PHMB associated craniofacial developmental toxicity under laboratory conditions, accompanied by oxidative stress related changes and altered Wnt related gene expression. General developmental toxicity may contribute to the craniofacial phenotype, and the partial pharmacological rescue does not establish pathway specific causality.

articles.title: 161Tb Radiopharmaceutical Therapy as a Treatment for RANKL-Positive Multiple Myeloma.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Denosumab, an anti-RANKL monoclonal antibody, is clinically approved for bone protection in multiple myeloma (MM) but lacks direct cytotoxic effects on tumor cells. Herein, we repurpose this well-tolerated antibody as a targeted delivery vehicle by conjugating it with the emerging radionuclide 161Tb, which emits low-energy conversion and Auger electrons with ultra-short tissue range, offering high relative biological effectiveness against single tumor cells and micrometastases. However, 161Tb-based radiopharmaceutical therapy has not been explored in MM. Our purpose is to evaluate the therapeutic potential of [161Tb]Tb-DOTA-Denosumab compared to [177Lu]Lu-DOTA-Denosumab for RANKL-positive MM. METHODS: DOTA-conjugated Denosumab was labeled with 161Tb and 177Lu. Radiochemical purity, in vitro stability and biodistribution were assessed. Therapeutic efficacy was evaluated in U266 and H929 subcutaneous xenograft models. Tumor volume, survival, body weight, hematologic, and biochemical parameters were monitored. Administered-activity-escalation toxicity studies were performed in tumor-free mice. RESULTS: Both radiolabeled conjugates showed high radiochemical purity (>95%), excellent in vitro stability and comparable tumor uptake. [161Tb]Tb-DOTA-Denosumab demonstrated significantly enhanced antitumor efficacy compared to [177Lu]Lu-DOTA-Denosumab at equivalent (1.85 MBq) or lower activities. In the U266 model, median survival was prolonged from 33 days (saline) to 45 days with 161Tb (1.85 MBq) versus 39 days with 177Lu (1.85 MBq). In the H929 model, median survival extended to 47 days with 161Tb (1.85 MBq) versus 31 days (saline) and 41 days with 177Lu (1.85 MBq). Toxicity studies confirmed reversible hematologic changes only at administered activities ≥3.70 MBq, with no severe organ damage. CONCLUSIONS: This is the first demonstration of 161Tb-based radiopharmaceutical therapy targeting RANKL in MM. [161Tb]Tb-DOTA-Denosumab exhibits superior antitumor efficacy and prolonged survival compared to its 177Lu-labeled counterpart. The unique Auger/conversion electron emission of 161Tb enables potent cytotoxicity against MM cells with favorable organ tolerability. These findings support 161Tb as a next-generation theranostic radionuclide for RANKL-positive malignancies and provide a strong rationale for clinical translation, highlighting the value of repurposing a clinically established antibody for radiopharmaceutical therapy.

articles.title: Development of sericin-elastin nanoblends containing resveratrol for cosmeceutical applications.
articles.abstract: Resveratrol (RSV), a high-value phytocompound upcycled from winemaking byproducts, is highly promising for cosmeceutical applications against oxidative stress due to its extraordinary antioxidant, anti-inflammatory and cytoprotective properties. However, its topical application is severely limited by chemical instability, poor aqueous solubility, and rapid degradation by light and oxygen. To overcome these limitations and maximize epidermal efficacy, a biocompatible nanoblend composed of sericin and elastin was developed. The sericin (4 mg/mL)/elastin (2 mg/mL) nanoblends showed an average diameter of 140 nm, a narrow size distribution, a Zeta potential of -35 mV and high stability at pH 7 and 10, as well as at temperatures between 32 °C and 37 °C. The encapsulation of RSV (0.4 mg/mL) did not affect the mean diameter and polydispersity index of the systems, allowing an entrapment efficiency of ∼30% (drug content of 0.12 mg/mL). The release profile showed a biphasic kinetic trend over time. When tested on HaCaT human keratinocytes, both single polymers and blend nanosystems demonstrated excellent tolerability, confirming the high biocompatibility of the formulation. Furthermore, RSV-loaded blend nanoparticles showed a superior cytoprotective effect compared to the free drug, a trend confirmed by DPPH, CellROX and MitoSOX assays. Finally, CompuSyn analysis validated a strong synergy between the carrier and RSV (CI < 1) with a synergistic effect at 10 µg/mL with a Dose Reduction Index (DRI) of 3.00. In conclusion, the developed sericin-elastin nanoblends containing RSV represent innovative cosmeceuticals characterized by strong antioxidant activity able to be employed for the topical treatment of skin disorders.

articles.title: CD44-targeted hyaluronic acid nanohydrogels enhance macrophage uptake and preserve the anti-inflammatory efficacy of dexamethasone.
articles.abstract: The inflammatory response is among the most critical drivers of tissue damage and systemic dysfunction. Although corticosteroids (CS) can achieve symptom remission and prevent tissue damage, systemic side effects are an issue due to the lack of targeted drug delivery. To this end, we propose a new approach to delivering CS via a hyaluronic acid (HA)-cholesterol nanohydrogel (NHs). Cholesterol, responsible for the formation of NHs, facilitates interactions with CS, while HA interacts with CD44, which is overexpressed on inflammatory cells. The aforementioned NHs were shown to efficiently load dexamethasone (DEX), with 75% drug entrapment efficiency without inducing cytotoxicity in the murine macrophage RAW 264.7 cell line. The ability of DEX to reduce inflammatory cytokine levels in lipopolysaccharide-activated RAW 264.7 cells remained intact when it was loaded into NHs. The empty NHs themselves exhibited anti-inflammatory activity, likely due to the high molecular weight of the HA used in the formulation. Finally, further investigation into the role of HA in immune cell uptake revealed significantly higher internalization by activated macrophages, driven by HA-CD44 interactions, which could enable improved cellular targeting. This nanohydrogel system offers a promising, easily manufactured, and highly biocompatible solution for anti-inflammatory drug delivery.

articles.title: Transfer learning-based multimodal prediction for efficient screening of afatinib co-amorphous systems.
articles.abstract: Most active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) are poorly water-soluble, limiting their pharmaceutical performance. Co-amorphous (CA) systems offer a promising formulation strategy, yet CA prediction remains constrained by limited labeled data and insufficient molecular representation. Here, a multimodal transfer-learning framework was developed by transferring molecular graph representations from a larger co-crystal dataset and integrating graph, DFT and SMILES information for small-sample CA prediction. The model achieved an AUC-ROC of 0.924 and an MCC of 0.771. Compared with existing AI-assisted CA prediction approaches, this framework combines cross-domain knowledge transfer with complementary molecular representations to address the limited-data challenge. Using afatinib (AF) as a model API, four AF-based CA systems were prepared by ball milling. Solid-state characterization supported amorphous CA formation, and dimer-level quantum-chemical calculations supported the plausibility of favorable local AF-co-former interaction motifs. The CA systems showed pH-dependent apparent solubility advantages and greater dissolution extents than Crystal AF. Under dry storage conditions, the CA systems maintained their amorphous state and morphology. CCK-8 assays revealed differences in HCC827 cell viability inhibition among the tested samples. Overall, this study establishes an AI-assisted approach for CA co-former screening and experimental prioritization, providing a practical strategy for formulation development of poorly soluble drugs.

articles.title: Glycocalyx-binding and cell-penetrating peptide-modified nanomicelles for enhanced ocular delivery of quercetin and retinal protection in a dAMD model.
articles.abstract: Dry age-related macular degeneration (dAMD) is a highly prevalent degenerative retinal disease. Quercetin, a bioactive ingredient in traditional Chinese medicine, can mitigate the oxidative stress that helps drive dAMD; however, its low water solubility and poor corneal permeability limit its efficacy. We developed dual-functional polymeric micelles (PMs) co-conjugated with a glycocalyx-binding peptide (GBP) and a cell-penetrating peptide (TAT) for the enhanced topical ocular delivery of quercetin (QUE), named GT-PMs/QUE. The GT-PMs/QUE exhibited a particle size of 46.25 ± 3.05 nm and a zeta potential of -5.64 ± 0.92 mV. GT-PMs exhibited significantly higher cellular uptake efficiency than the unmodified group (PMs) and single-peptide modified groups (GBP-PMs and TAT-PMs). In the sodium iodate-induced oxidative damage model of adult retinal pigment epithelial cell line-19 (ARPE-19) cells, the GT-PMs/QUE treatment group showed significantly reduced ROS and MDA levels along with markedly increased SOD, CAT, and GSH activities that approached normal control levels compared to the model group. In a mouse model of dAMD, GT-PMs/QUE greatly improved the bioavailability of quercetin delivered via eye drop administration and attenuated sodium iodate-induced retinal damage. This study provides a theoretical and experimental basis for enhanced ocular delivery of quercetin and protection against dAMD-related retinal damage.

articles.title: Are we selecting the right model compounds for advanced formulation research?
articles.abstract: Numerous advanced-formulation papers begin with the same problem statement: "30-40% of marketed drugs, 70-75% of clinical candidates and 90% of new chemical entities are poorly soluble in water". However, these figures are not fully supported by data and citations. We traced these numbers back to their original sources and reassessed them against the current API landscape. The 30-40% value was derived from a 2006 analysis of top selling drugs. Reassessing the top selling drugs in 2025 reveals a marked increase: about 55% of the orally administered small molecules now fall into the practically insoluble category. The 70-75% and 90% claims could only be traced to conference presentations and a review abstract with no underlying data. We further argue that the Biopharmaceutics Classification System categorization is not an intrinsic property of an API since it shifts depending on dose, particle size and formulation, i.e., no compound can be classified without considering the formulation and dose. A Scopus analysis showed that the APIs most frequently used as poorly soluble model compounds are the NSAIDs, antifungals and compounds, such as carbamazepine, carvedilol and simvastatin. The majority of these "poorly solubles" are in fact completely absorbed in vivo with no solubility issues at all. As more relevant alternatives to the above-mentioned compounds, we propose and briefly review ten marketed non-oncology APIs with unresolved dissolution and solubility limitations that would make better model compounds for advanced formulation research.

articles.title: A GLP-1/apelin dual receptor agonist shows neuroprotective effects in the MPTP mouse model of Parkinson's disease.
articles.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a chronic disorder with no disease-modifying treatment available. The glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) class of drugs is on the market to treat diabetes and obesity. GLP-1 drugs have also shown neuroprotective effects in animal models and clinical trials in PD patients. Apelin (APJ) is an adipokine peptide hormone with neuroprotective actions in preclinical studies. Here, we test the effects of a rationally designed bifunctional peptide, namely ELA (exendin-4-linker-apelin), in the MPTP mouse model of PD. The single GLP-1 receptor agonist liraglutide was used as a comparator. Motor activity was improved by both drugs (open field, pole test, Rotarod), and the inflammation response was reduced (activation of microglia and astrocytes, pro-inflammatory cytokine levels). In addition, synapse numbers were improved in the striatum (Golgi strain, TEM), expression of synapse-associated proteins was enhanced, alongside reduced expression of genes that increase mitochondrial fission. Mitochondrial fusion gene expressions (Opa1, Mfn2, Drp1) and mitochondrial morphology were also normalized (TEM). ELA was superior to liraglutide in some, but not all, parameters measured. The results suggest that the rational design of bifunctional peptides targeting both GLP-1 and APJ pathways-with optimized pharmacokinetics and enhanced blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability-merits further investigation as a strategy for developing more effective treatments for PD.

articles.title: NuPath, a higher-sensitivity TRUPATH-derived biosensor, expands detection of basal and agonist-induced GPCR activation.
articles.abstract: Bioluminescence resonance energy transfer (BRET) biosensors allow direct quantification of heterotrimeric G protein activation downstream of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), although restricted dynamic range can limit the detection of subtle, subunit-specific, or constitutively active signalling. We engineered NuPath, a TRUPATH-based biosensor in which Renilla luciferase 8 (RLuc8) within Gα was substituted with NanoLuc luciferase (nLuc) and enhanced yellow fluorescent protein (eYFP) replaced green fluorescent protein 2 (GFP2) fused to Gγ, while preserving the original sensor insertion architecture. NuPath is adapted for use in conventional 96-well plate format and supports direct, no-transfer readouts after receptor expression, whether receptors are introduced transiently or via stable cell lines, thereby simplifying experimental procedures. Side-by-side comparisons of matched NuPath and TRUPATH systems were performed across six GPCRs, Gαi2, GαOA, GαsL, and Gα11, and a range of Gβγ dimers. NuPath produced approximately 3- to 14-fold greater maximal agonist responses with Gαi2, GαsL, and Gα11, whereas GαOA sensors produced responses of broadly comparable magnitude with lower variability. The broadened dynamic range uncovered receptor-dependent variations in Gβγ pairing that were largely undetectable in TRUPATH measurements. NuPath further enabled detection of inverse agonist-mediated suppression of constitutive signalling at the growth hormone secretagogue receptor (GHSR) by liver-expressed antimicrobial peptide 2 (LEAP2), an effect not discernible using TRUPATH. AlphaFold 3 structural models suggested reduced donor-acceptor separation and diminished displacement of the Gα α-helical domain in NuPath compared with equivalent TRUPATH complexes. Collectively, these results position NuPath as a robust, modular enhancement of TRUPATH for resolving agonist-driven, Gβγ-specific, and constitutive GPCR signalling.

articles.title: Alnustone ameliorates atopic dermatitis by rebalancing TAp63/ΔNp63 to upregulate filaggrin and restore skin barrier function.
articles.abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic, pruritic, erythematous skin condition with skin barrier dysfunction, driven largely by filaggrin (FLG) deficiency; however, direct FLG-targeting therapeutics remains lacking. To identify novel natural products capable of enhancing FLG expression, we screened an in-house natural product library using a dual-luciferase reporter assay in HaCaT keratinocytes, which revealed that alnustone dose-dependently activated the human FLG promoter. RT-qPCR and Western blot analysis confirmed that alnustone upregulated FLG mRNA and protein levels in keratinocytes, independently of the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR). The therapeutic efficacy of alnustone was evaluated in oxazolone-induced AD mouse model, where topical application significantly alleviated clinical severity, inflammation, and skin barrier defects. The molecular mechanism was explored using ChIP-seq data mining, isoform-specific modulation, promoter truncation, and DNA pull-down assays. The results demostrated that alnustone rebalanced p63 isoforms by downregulating the transcriptional repressor TAp63 and upregulating the transcriptional activator ΔNp63. Both isoforms directly bound to a core response element (-390/-381) within the FLG promoter to mediate its transcriptional activation. To our knowledge, alnustone represents the first barrier-repair agent that ameliorates AD by transcriptionally upregulating FLG via restoring TAp63/ΔNp63 homeostasis, offering a novel therapeutic strategy targeting skin barrier regeneration in AD.

articles.title: Aripiprazole collapses metabolic plasticity through the GNAQ/RXRα/MCT4 axis in colorectal cancer.
articles.abstract: Metabolic plasticity enables colorectal cancer (CRC) cells to adapt to energy stress by dynamically adjusting the relative contributions of oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) and glycolysis, thereby contributing to tumor progression and therapeutic resistance. However, pharmacological strategies capable of disrupting this metabolic flexibility remain limited. Here, we identify aripiprazole, an approved antipsychotic drug with emerging anticancer activity, as a disruptor of metabolic plasticity in CRC. Aripiprazole impaired mitochondrial function, reduced OXPHOS-derived ATP production, and initially triggered compensatory glycolytic activation. However, this adaptive response was not sustained, as aripiprazole suppressed monocarboxylate transporter 4 (MCT4), a key lactate transporter involved in glycolytic adaptation under hypoxic stress. Functional experiments showed that MCT4 overexpression attenuated aripiprazole-induced growth inhibition and apoptosis, whereas MCT4 knockdown sensitized CRC cells to hypoxic stress. Mechanistically, RXRα acted as a negative regulator of MCT4. Aripiprazole disrupted the interaction between GNAQ and RXRα, promoted nuclear accumulation of RXRα, thereby repressing MCT4 expression. This blockade of MCT4-dependent glycolytic compensation, together with mitochondrial dysfunction, resulted in ATP depletion and apoptotic cell death in CRC cells. Collectively, our findings reveal a previously unrecognized GNAQ/RXRα/MCT4 signaling axis that sustains metabolic plasticity in CRC and demonstrate that aripiprazole can pharmacologically disrupt this adaptive program. These results provide mechanistic insight into the anticancer activity of aripiprazole and support targeting metabolic plasticity as a therapeutic strategy for CRC.

articles.title: Vasorelaxant and Antihypertensive Effects of Salicylaldehyde: Involvement of Renin-Angiotensin System and Calcium/Potassium Channel Modulation.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Natural products are widely used in traditional medicine for managing cardiovascular disorders, including hypertension. Salicylaldehyde, a naturally occurring aromatic aldehyde found in plant-derived preparations, remains poorly characterized regarding its vascular effects. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to evaluate the vasorelaxant and antihypertensive properties of salicylaldehyde and to elucidate its underlying mechanisms of action. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Molecular docking was performed to assess interactions with key vascular targets. In vitro vasorelaxant activity was investigated using isolated rat thoracic aortic rings precontracted with epinephrine (EP, 10 μM) or potassium chloride (KCl, 80 mM). The involvement of endothelium-dependent and independent pathways was examined using pharmacological inhibitors and angiotensin II-induced contraction assays. In vivo effects were evaluated following oral administration of salicylaldehyde (20 and 40 mg/kg) in normotensive and N-nitro-L-arginine methyl ester (L-NAME)-induced hypertensive rats. Blood pressure was measured using a tail-cuff system during acute (6 h) and sub-chronic (7 days) treatments. RESULTS: Salicylaldehyde showed strong binding affinities toward angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) and angiotensin II Type 1 Receptor. It induced concentration-dependent vasorelaxation, significantly reduced after endothelial removal and under KCl-induced contraction. Its effects were attenuated by inhibitors of ACE, ACE2, ATP-sensitive K+ channels, and L-type calcium channels, and it inhibited angiotensin II-induced contraction. In vivo, it significantly reduced systolic and diastolic blood pressure in hypertensive rats. CONCLUSION: Salicylaldehyde exerts antihypertensive effects via multiple mechanisms and may contribute to the cardiovascular activity of plant-derived remedies.

articles.title: Impact of nonspecific binding to membrane vesicles on unbound IC50 estimation for P-glycoprotein and breast cancer resistance protein inhibitors and implications for drug-drug interaction risk assessment.
articles.abstract: P-glycoprotein and breast cancer resistance protein are key efflux transporters relevant to drug-drug interactions (DDIs) for orally administered drugs. The International Council for Harmonisation of Technical Requirements for Pharmaceuticals for Human Use M12 guidance recommends using unbound in vitro inhibition potency (IC50,u) for clinical risk assessment, yet the influence of nonspecific binding to membrane vesicles remains uncharacterized. Herein, vesicle binding for a panel of efflux transporter inhibitors was systematically quantified using equilibrium dialysis and compared with conventional microsomal binding. Nonspecific binding to vesicles reduced free inhibitor concentrations, resulting in right-shifted IC50 values, particularly for high-binding compounds (itraconazole and dronedarone) compared with low-binding compounds (telmisartan) in breast cancer resistance protein assays with Sf9 control vesicles. Similar right shifts were observed for P-glycoprotein inhibition assays with human embryonic kidney 293 control vesicles, although less pronounced. Correction of IC50 values across different vesicle concentrations generally resulted in aligned IC50,u values. Microsomal binding correlated strongly (Pearson correlation coefficient = 0.965) with vesicle binding, supporting its use as a surrogate for binding correction. Incorporating binding-corrected IC50 values into static DDI risk calculations increased false positives but did not affect false negatives. These findings demonstrate that accounting for fraction unbound in vesicle-based assays can substantially influence the estimation of in vitro inhibitory potency and subsequent static DDI risk assessment. SIGNIFICANT STATEMENT: This study systematically characterizes nonspecific binding to membrane vesicles in P-glycoprotein and breast cancer resistance protein inhibition assays and demonstrates its substantial impact on IC50 determination. The strong correlation between vesicles and microsomal binding provides a practical surrogate for implementing International Council for Harmonisation of Technical Requirements for Pharmaceuticals for Human Use M12 unbound potency recommendations for vesicle-based inhibition assays.

articles.title: Functional characterization of rare DPYD variants identified in 8,380 Japanese individuals: implications for 5-fluorouracil metabolism.
articles.abstract: Dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase (DPD) is the rate-limiting enzyme in the metabolism of 5-fluorouracil, and reduced DPD activity resulting from DPYD genetic variants is a major cause of severe 5-fluorouracil -induced toxicity. Although several clinically relevant variants have been identified in Caucasian populations, the functional consequences of rare DPYD variants identified in Japanese individuals remain poorly characterized. In this study, we comprehensively analyzed 26 DPYD variants identified through whole-genome sequencing of 8380 Japanese individuals. Recombinant DPD proteins were expressed in 293FT cells, and enzymatic activity was evaluated using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry to determine kinetic parameters (Km, Vmax, CLint). Protein expression levels and quaternary structure were assessed by immunoblotting and blue native PAGE, and structural modeling was performed to explore possible structural consequences of selected variants. Among the 26 DPD variants analyzed, 5 exhibited markedly reduced or abolished enzymatic activity compared with wild-type DPD, including 3 loss of function variants. Loss of detectable homodimer formation was observed in Gly194Asp and Glu386Ter, whereas other functionally impaired variants retained homodimer formation, indicating that altered dimerization represents only one potential mechanism contributing to DPD dysfunction. Structural analyses suggested possible local alterations affecting cofactor interactions or the dimer interface in selected variants, providing hypotheses for future mechanistic investigation. These findings provide a comprehensive functional characterization of rare DPYD variants identified in Japanese individuals and support their prioritization for future clinical validation. However, their clinical significance and potential utility for fluoropyrimidine dose individualization require confirmation in patients receiving fluoropyrimidine-based chemotherapy. SIGNIFICANT STATEMENT: This study functionally characterized 26 rare DPYD variants identified in a Japanese population and identified 5 variants with markedly reduced or abolished DPD activity. These findings expand the functional annotation of DPYD variation in a population in which established fluoropyrimidine-associated risk variants are uncommon and provide evidence to prioritize functionally impaired variants for future clinical validation.

articles.title: Redox-mitochondrial-epigenetic network disruption and its intergenerational impact in zebrafish: Protective effects of metformin.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Oxidative stress is a central mechanism of chronic toxicity, disrupting metabolic, inflammatory, apoptotic, mitochondrial, and epigenetic processes. Potassium bromate (KBrO₃) induces oxidative stress, but its systemic effects following chronic exposure and modulation by metformin remain insufficiently characterized. This study evaluated chronic KBrO₃ toxicity in zebrafish, the effects of concurrent metformin exposure, and molecular responses in F1 offspring following parental exposure. METHODS: Adult zebrafish were exposed to KBrO₃ for 28 days with or without metformin co-treatment. Histopathological analyses of liver, ovary, intestine, and testis were performed. IL-1β, insulin, and vitellogenin were analyzed by ELISA, wheras oxidative stress, metabolic, inflammatory, apoptotic, and epigenetic markers by qPCR. Global DNA methylation, mitochondrial DNA copy number, and relative telomere length were evaluated in F0 and F1 cohorts. Data were analyzed using conventional statistics, principal component analysis, and Spearman correlation. RESULTS: KBrO₃ exposure was associated with alterations in antioxidant defence, metabolism, inflammation, apoptosis, mitochondrial and epigenetic endpoints, and tissue pathology. Metformin co-treatment attenuated multiple KBrO₃-associated molecular and histopathological alterations. In F1 offspring, selected gene-expression and DNA methylation alterations were observed, whereas mtDNA copy number and relative telomere length did not differ significantly among groups, indicating endpoint-specific intergenerational responses. Multivariate analyses identified coordinated biomarker patterns associated with treatment. CONCLUSION: Chronic KBrO₃ exposure produced coordinated molecular and tissue alterations, while metformin co-treatment attenuated several associated responses. Selected F1 molecular and epigenetic alterations indicate intergenerational responses following parental exposure, although F2/F3 generations were not assessed. These findings support further investigation of metformin as a pharmacological modulator of oxidative stress-associated toxicity.

articles.title: Insights into osteoporosis triggered by common antiepileptic drugs via network toxicology, molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Antiepileptic drugs (AEDs), first-line treatments for epilepsy and related seizure disorders, are increasingly recognized as important risk factors for osteoporosis. However, the molecular mechanisms and specific targets underlying AED-induced bone loss remain largely unclear. METHODS: We explored these mechanisms using an integrated strategy combining network toxicology, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and in vitro experiments. Common targets of four AEDs and osteoporosis were identified through database screening, followed by protein-protein interaction network construction, hub gene identification, and functional enrichment analysis. Molecular docking was used to evaluate the predicted binding affinity between AEDs and primary hub targets, and 100-ns molecular dynamics simulations were applied to assess dynamic binding stability. Furthermore, colony formation assays and Western blots were performed in MC3T3-E1 pre-osteoblasts to support the computational predictions. RESULTS: We identified 47, 50, 46, and 48 potential osteoporosis-related targets for carbamazepine phenobarbital phenytoin (PHT), and valproic acid respectively. These targets were mainly enriched in key signaling pathways and cellular processes associated with bone metabolism. Topological analysis identified four primary hub targets: epidermal growth factor receptor, CASP3, peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma, and PTGS2. AEDs and their targets exhibited favorable binding affinity in the molecular docking simulations (binding energy < -5 kcal/mol). Molecular dynamics simulations revealed heterogeneous dynamic stability among the complexes: PB-CASP3 and PHT-PPARG reached relatively stable conformational equilibrium, whereas CBZ-EGFR displayed notable protein residue flexibility in the equilibrated trajectory, and VPA-PTGS2 sustained persistent structural fluctuations during the simulation period. In vitro experiments demonstrated that all AEDs inhibited the clonogenic capacity of MC3T3-E1 cells, and Western blot results further indicated that AEDs differentially modulated the expression and activation levels of their corresponding primary hub targets, which was consistent with the computational predictions. CONCLUSION: This study constructs an integrated research framework combining computational prediction and in vitro validation to explore potential molecular mechanisms underlying AED-induced osteoblast dysfunction and osteoporosis. The findings highlight candidate targets and provide a preliminary mechanistic basis for future rational clinical medication and skeletal protection in patients receiving long-term AED therapy.

articles.title: Targeting the PCSK9-PR-IL-17 axis for psoriasis therapy.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Psoriasis is a chronic, immune-mediated inflammatory dermatosis characterized by keratinocyte hyperproliferation and systemic metabolic comorbidities. Although proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) is a well-established regulator of lipid metabolism, its role in the cutaneous inflammatory microenvironment remains poorly defined. This study investigated the contribution of PCSK9 to psoriatic inflammation and its potential underlying mechanisms. METHODS: PCSK9 expression was assessed in human psoriatic lesions and an imiquimod (IMQ)-induced mouse model. The effects of pharmacological PCSK9 inhibition with SBC-110736 were evaluated using PASI-like scores and inflammatory cell infiltration. Transcriptomic analysis was performed to identify associated signaling pathways. The relationship between PCSK9 and progesterone receptor (PR) expression in keratinocytes and the effects of the PR agonist progesterone were also examined. RESULTS: PCSK9 expression was significantly upregulated in human psoriatic lesions and in the IMQ-induced mouse model. SBC-110736 attenuated psoriasis-like disease severity, reducing PASI-like scores and infiltration of CD4+ and CD11b+ cells. Transcriptomic analysis indicated that PCSK9 inhibition primarily suppressed interleukin-17 (IL-17) signaling while restoring Pgr expression. PCSK9 and PR expression were inversely associated in keratinocytes, suggesting that PCSK9-mediated PR downregulation may exacerbate IL-17-driven inflammation. Progesterone treatment produced similar therapeutic effects to those observed with PCSK9 inhibition. DISCUSSION: These findings suggest that a PCSK9-PR-IL-17 axis contributes to psoriasis pathogenesis, with PR potentially serving as an endogenous anti-inflammatory brake. Targeting this pathway may offer a strategy to modulate cutaneous inflammation, while its potential effects on related metabolic disturbances warrant further investigation.

articles.title: Berberine suppresses mechanical stretch-induced apoptosis and proliferation in vascular smooth muscle cells via ROS/PDI/Drp1 signaling pathway.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) exhibit heterogeneous responses to mechanical stretch stress (SS), with some undergoing apoptosis and others proliferating. The mechanisms underlying this differential fate decision remain unclear. OBJECTIVE: This study investigated whether SS-induced heterogeneity in F-actin expression dictates distinct mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS) responses, leading to different VSMC fates, and evaluated the therapeutic potential of the berberine (BBR). METHODS: VSMCs were subjected to SS. F-actin heterogeneity was characterized, and mitochondrial ROS (mtROS), proliferation, and apoptosis were assessed. The involvement of the PKCα/PDI/Drp1 signaling axis was examined using pharmacological inhibitors and BBR. RESULTS: SS induced heterogeneous mtROS production in VSMCs with varying F-actin levels. This differential ROS signaling concurrently activated the pro-proliferative mTOR/p70 pathway and the pro-apoptotic caspase-9/3 cascade via the PKCα/PDI/Drp1 axis. Importantly, BBR treatment effectively attenuated both SS-induced proliferation and apoptosis by suppressing PKCα activation and subsequent mitochondrial signaling. CONCLUSION: Our findings reveal that F-actin heterogeneity determines VSMC fate under SS by driving distinct mitochondrial ROS responses. BBR, by counteracting these ROS-dependent pathways, emerges as a promising therapeutic strategy for managing stretch-related vascular pathologies, such as hypertension-induced atherosclerosis.

articles.title: High-affinity ELR+ CXC chemokines display balanced G protein-, GRK- and β-arrestin-associated transducer engagement at the viral G protein-coupled receptor ORF74.
articles.abstract: Open reading frame 74 (ORF74) is the single G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) encoded in the genome of Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV). Due to its high constitutive activity and broad chemokine binding profile, ORF74 contributes to KSHV-associated diseases through autocrine and paracrine mechanisms that promote cell proliferation, inflammation and angiogenesis. Previous studies showed that ELR+ CXC chemokines (i.e., CXCL1-3 and CXCL5-8), which contain a conserved Glu-Leu-Arg motif, bind ORF74 with high affinity. Among these chemokines, CXCL1-3 and CXCL6-8 act as full or partial agonists in ORF74-mediated G protein signaling and β-arrestin recruitment, whereas CXCL5 behaves as a neutral ligand. However, whether these chemokines preferentially engage specific intracellular transducers remains unclear. We therefore applied a unified NanoLuc Binary Technology (NanoBiT) platform in HEK293A cells to systematically compare how ELR+ CXC chemokines modulate ORF74-transducer proximity across the G protein-GRK-β-arrestin axis. CXCL1-3 and CXCL6-8, but not CXCL5, induced concentration-dependent ORF74-specific responses involving miniGi recruitment, Gβ1 proximity, GRK2/3/5/6 proximity and β-arrestin1/2 recruitment. Using CXCL1 as the reference ligand, bias analysis showed that the active ELR+ CXC chemokines engage ORF74 in a largely balanced manner across these proximal transducer readouts.

articles.title: Exploratory pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic range of tigecycline for balancing treatment effect and safety in hospital-acquired pneumonia: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Tigecycline (TGC) is a core antibiotic for treating hospital-acquired pneumonia (HAP) caused by multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria, but the absence of individualized dosing guidance that balances treatment effect and safety frequently results in suboptimal efficacy or coagulation-related adverse events in clinical practice. METHODS: A single-center retrospective study was conducted, enrolling 100 patients with MDR-HAP who were assigned to a standard-dose group or a high-dose group based on clinical decisions. The efficacy and safety of different TGC dosing regimens were compared between the two groups. RESULTS: The trough concentration (Cmin), intermediate concentration (C1/2), and peak concentration (Cmax), the estimated ratio of the area under the concentration-time curve to the 24h of dosing/minimum inhibitory concentration (eAUIC), pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) target attainment rate, clinical response rate and overall favorable outcome rate in the high-dose group were significantly higher than those in the standard group (p < 0.05). The incidence of thrombocytopenia was significantly higher in the high-dose group (36.67% vs. 17.14%, p = 0.034), whereas the incidence of hypofibrinogenemia was numerically higher but did not reach statistical significance (40.0% vs. 30.0%, p = 0.330). No significant between-group differences were observed in microbiological eradication rate, median survival time, 30-day all-cause mortality, coagulation parameters, gastrointestinal reactions, or liver function damage. Binary logistic regression analysis revealed that eAUIC [OR = 1.394 (1.135-1.712), p = 0.002] was an influencing predictor associated with clinical treatment effect. The area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve for eAUIC was 0.813, with a maximum Youden index of 0.557. The corresponding critical value was determined to be 2.915, with a sensitivity of 96.9% and a specificity of 58.8%. Furthermore, eAUIC was independently associated with both hypofibrinogenemia and thrombocytopenia. We identified an exploratory candidate eAUIC range of 2.915 - 3.565 that was associated with both clinical treatment effect and coagulation-related adverse events. DISCUSSION: This eAUIC range was derived from retrospective data and should be framed explicitly as a hypothesis to be tested, clinical applicability requires confirmation through prospective studies and external validation. Therapeutic drug monitoring may assist in optimizing therapy, but prospective studies are needed to confirm these observations.

articles.title: Interpretable machine learning classifies β-lactamase subclasses and prioritizes boundary variants for antimicrobial resistance surveillance.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Antimicrobial resistance is a major global health threat, and β-lactamase-mediated inactivation of β-lactam antibiotics remains a leading cause of treatment failure. Rapid identification of emerging β-lactamase variants and improved understanding of their functional diversity are therefore essential for resistance surveillance and therapeutic development. METHODS: Here, we developed an interpretable machine learning framework to classify major Class A β-lactamase subclasses (TEM, SHV, and CTX-M) and distinguish them from non-β-lactamase hydrolases using multidimensional protein descriptors. Descriptors based on sequence composition, physicochemical properties, residue accessibility, and structural topology were evaluated to identify a minimal panel of 30 descriptors while preserving biological interpretability. RESULTS: The selected descriptors provided strong discriminatory power and were linked to steric environment, hydrophobicity, flexibility, solvent exposure, and residue interaction patterns, consistent with roles in substrate recognition and catalysis. Projection into reduced descriptor space identified transitional variants near subclass boundaries, including CTX-M/SHV convergence zones and non-β-lactamase hydrolases with partial β-lactamase-like signatures. Representative case studies indicated that some apparent misclassifications may reflect annotation inconsistencies, scaffold convergence, or early adaptive trajectories, highlighting candidates for experimental follow-up. External validation using 271 independent proteins annotated as non-β-lactamase hydrolases demonstrated 96.95% specificity, with only limited false-positive assignments. Most incorrect classifications showed weak statistical support, indicating that confidence filtering could further improve screening performance. DISCUSSION: Overall, this study demonstrates that compact descriptor-based models can provide accurate and interpretable classification of β-lactamase-related proteins while identifying emerging boundary variants relevant to antimicrobial resistance surveillance. The framework offers a scalable approach for protein annotation, monitoring resistance evolution, and supporting future inhibitor development.

articles.title: Value-based pricing of brensocatib for frequently exacerbating non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis in China: a China-adapted, FEV1-inclusive time-dependent markov analysis.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To estimate a China-specific value-based annual price (P*) for brensocatib 25 mg added to standard care (SC), compared with SC alone, in adults with frequently exacerbating non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis, and to assess how strongly the estimate depends on transferred assumptions linking forced expiratory volume in 1 s (FEV1) to long-term outcomes. METHODS: A seven-state Markov cohort model with monthly cycles and a lifetime horizon was constructed from the Chinese healthcare system perspective. Chinese sources informed the target population, exacerbation burden, baseline microbiology, background mortality, resource use, costs, discounting, and decision context, while ASPEN supplied the exacerbation rate ratio (0.81) and annual FEV1 decline (24 mL with brensocatib 25 mg vs. 62 mL with placebo). In the base case, cohort-mean FEV1 was linked to utility and mortality through explicit external mappings. A prespecified structural sensitivity removed both mappings but retained the trial-observed exacerbation benefit. Costs and outcomes were discounted by 4.5% annually. The primary willingness-to-pay (WTP) threshold was CNY 200,000 per quality-adjusted life-year (QALY); uncertainty was examined with a paired 10,000-draw probabilistic sensitivity analysis (PSA). RESULTS: At an illustrative price of CNY 120,000/year, the FEV1-inclusive base case estimated an incremental cost of CNY 551,543, gains of 0.2761 QALYs and 0.3432 discounted life-years, and 0.57 fewer lifetime exacerbations. These results corresponded to an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio of CNY 1,997,665/QALY and P* of CNY 11,692/year. Drug acquisition accounted for almost all of the incremental cost. The PSA median P* was CNY 11,611/year (95% simulation interval CNY 4,145-19,324), and none of 10,000 simulations was cost-effective at CNY 120,000/year for WTP thresholds up to CNY 300,000/QALY. Estimates changed little when China-specific demographic and exacerbation inputs were varied. In contrast, removing the FEV1-linked pathway reduced P* to CNY 990/year, while assuming persistent efficacy after attrition increased it to CNY 24,432/year. CONCLUSION: With inputs localised wherever credible Chinese evidence was available, the FEV1-inclusive base case estimated P* at CNY 11,692/year for a WTP of CNY 200,000/QALY. The broad pricing implication was stable, although the exact estimate depended chiefly on the durability and downstream consequences of the 52-week FEV1 difference. Both the base case and the key structural sensitivity remained far below the illustrative annual price of CNY 120,000.

articles.title: APOE4 differentially alters lipid composition in extracellular vesicles from hiPSC-derived neurons of Alzheimer's disease patients.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The Apolipoprotein E4 (APOE4) is the most significant genetic risk factor for late-onset Alzheimer's disease (AD), but the cellular mechanisms by which it increases vulnerability remain poorly understood. Lipids play a crucial role in membrane organization, vesicle trafficking, and inflammatory signaling in the brain. Increasing evidence suggests that changes in lipid metabolism might serve as a connection between genetic risk and neurodegeneration. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) reflect the lipidomic composition of their parent cell offering a window into lipidomic alterations that may be tracked in living humans over time. Given high variability in human samples, we sought to define APOE4-related lipidomic EV signatures in a controlled human cellular system. METHODS: We studied EVs secreted by four replicates of human-induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived glutamatergic neurons from two healthy individuals (APOE2/E3 and APOE4/4) and two patients with AD (APOE3/3 and APOE4/4). Targeted lipidomics enabled quantitative profiling of hundreds of individual lipid species across major lipid classes. Univariate and multivariate analyses were applied to identify lipid alterations associated with APOE genotype and AD status. RESULTS: APOE4 was associated with differences in lipid composition in neuronal EVs from both healthy and AD donors, suggesting that APOE4 influences EV lipid composition regardless of AD. Additionally, APOE4/4 carriers with AD exhibited clear, species-specific lipid imbalances. Lower levels of ganglioside GM3 and higher of phosphatidylserine emerged as consistent contributors to the APOE4-associated AD lipid signature, alongside alterations in dihydrosphingomyelin and phosphatidylinositol species linked to membrane integrity, endolysosomal function, and inflammatory pathways. These lipid species were among the strongest variables distinguishing healthy and AD APOE4/4 samples in multivariate analyses. CONCLUSION: These findings specify lipidomic changes in AD related to the APOE4 genotype, and support a model by which APOE4 creates a lipid profile that becomes selectively dysregulated in AD. By identifying specific lipid species associated with APOE4 and AD, this work provides further evidence that distinct lipidomic signatures are associated with both APOE4 and AD. These findings may contribute to the identification of lipid-based biomarkers and support future investigations into genotype-informed therapeutic strategies, although validation in larger, independent cohorts is required.

articles.title: Rituximab with low-dose glucocorticoids for treating refractory membranous nephropathy: a prospective single-center cohort study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Rituximab (RTX) is the first-line treatment for primary membranous nephropathy (pMN), yet approximately one-third of patients exhibit refractory disease. Evidence supporting RTX combined with low-dose glucocorticoids for refractory pMN remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of this combination regimen in a rituximab-naïve refractory cohort. METHODS: Thirty-six adults with refractory pMN received rituximab plus low-dose glucocorticoids (prednisone equivalent). The primary endpoint was clinical remission at 24 months, analyzed in both the intention-to-treat (ITT, n = 36) and per-protocol (PP, n = 22) populations. Sensitivity analyses included a worst-case scenario (assuming all dropouts were non-remitters). RESULTS: Thirty-five patients had evaluable 12-month outcomes, and 26 of them achieved remission (74.3%, with 25.7% achieving complete remission and 48.6% partial remission). By 24 months, the remission rate was 95.5% (21/22) in the per-protocol analysis and 91.67% in the intention-to-treat analysis, compared with 58.3% (21/36) in the worst-case scenario. We found no statistically significant difference in cumulative remission rates between serum PLA2R-positive and PLA2R-negative groups, or between renal tissue PLA2R-positive and PLA2R-negative groups. All 25 patients positive for anti-PLA2R antibodies showed a decreasing antibody trend after treatment, and 80.0% (20/25) achieved complete antibody clearance (antibody titer <20 RU/mL). Adverse events occurred in 37.1% (13/35) of patients, with 11.4% (4/35) of patients developing serious infections. No serious malignant events or fatal events were reported during the study. CONCLUSION: In this cohort of patients with refractory pMN, rituximab combined with low-dose glucocorticoids achieved high short-term remission rates, and no safety signals were observed that would preclude further investigation. However, given the uncontrolled study design, repeated RTX dosing, and residual confounding from prior immunosuppression, we cannot draw definitive conclusions on whether adding glucocorticoids offers incremental benefit compared with rituximab monotherapy. The high remission rates observed in this study may also be attributable to repeated rituximab exposure and residual effects of prior immunosuppression. Furthermore, this empirical combination regimen was not designed to test whether glucocorticoids have a direct additive or synergistic effect. Larger randomized controlled trials are therefore warranted to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Ocular safety signals of sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor modulators in postmarketing surveillance.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P) receptor modulators are used for immune-mediated diseases, and macular oedema is an established ocular adverse effect. However, ocular-focused, class-wide postmarketing reporting across all five approved agents remains incompletely characterized. METHODS: We analyzed U.S. Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) data from 2004 Q1 through 2026 Q1 using report-level deduplication, approval-aligned windows, and primary-suspect exposure. Ocular events were assessed using a curated set of 52 Preferred Term (PT) strings. Sensitivity analyses included report-level macular/retinal oedema aggregation, same-indication active comparators, temporal and sparse-data analyses, restricted empirical-Bayes assessment, and external validation in Canada Vigilance. Exact-date time to onset was assessed for the aggregated phenotype. RESULTS: The primary cohort included 98,843 primary-suspect reports, of which 8,812 (8.9%) were ocular, representing 12,088 unique ocular report-PT pairs. At the class level, 21 ocular PTs met primary signal criteria; macular oedema showed the strongest anatomically specific signal (n = 947; reporting odds ratio [ROR], 48.18; 95% confidence interval [CI], 44.84-51.76). Fingolimod had the broadest signal spectrum; macular oedema was the principal anatomically specific signal for siponimod and ozanimod. No ponesimod PT met primary criteria, and the etrasimod macular oedema estimate was sparse (n = 11). Of 36 primary drug-PT signals, 13 were High, 22 Moderate, and one Low. Report-level aggregation yielded a class-level ROR of 29.47 (95% CI, 27.62-31.45). In indication-restricted multiple sclerosis analyses, the association remained elevated versus all non-S1P disease-modifying therapies (ROR, 43.85; 95% CI, 35.75-53.78), while ulcerative colitis/inflammatory bowel disease analyses were sparse and exploratory. For fingolimod, the association persisted after exclusion of the first two post-approval years (ROR, 45.79; 95% CI, 37.26-56.26). Median time to onset was 93.0 days for fingolimod and 15.5 days for siponimod. Canada Vigilance showed a concordant class-level association (ROR, 74.00; 95% CI, 59.30-92.35). CONCLUSION: Macular/retinal oedema was the most consistent ocular reporting pattern in the S1P receptor modulator class. The association remained evident after phenotype aggregation and indication-restricted analysis and was also observed in Canada Vigilance. Sparse data for newer agents and residual confounding limit comparative interpretation.

articles.title: Interaction of major monoterpenes from Rosmarinus officinalis L. essential oil with the human serotonin transporter: molecular docking, radioligand binding, and functional uptake studies.
articles.abstract: Major depressive disorder remains a leading cause of disability worldwide, and current antidepressants are limited by delayed therapeutic onset, incomplete efficacy, and adverse effects. Although Rosmarinus officinalis L. essential oil and its major monoterpenes exhibit antidepressant-like and anxiolytic properties, their molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated whether the principal rosemary monoterpenes, α-pinene, camphor, and 1,8-cineole, directly interact with the human serotonin transporter (hSERT) and its functional effects. Molecular docking simulations targeting the orthosteric (S1) and allosteric (S2) binding sites were combined with [3H]-paroxetine binding displacement assays and SERT-mediated uptake experiments based on the fluorescent serotonin analog FFN246 in HEK293 cells expressing YFP-tagged hSERT. Docking analyses predicted plausible binding poses for all three monoterpenes within both the S1 and S2 regions, although with less favorable docking scores than fluoxetine. Radioligand displacement assays provided experimental evidence that all three compounds interact with hSERT, producing concentration-dependent displacement of [3H]-paroxetine, with α-pinene displaying the highest potency, followed by 1,8-cineole and camphor. Functional assays further showed that all monoterpenes produced significant but incomplete inhibition of transporter-mediated FFN246 uptake, even at high micromolar concentrations, indicating partial rather than complete transporter blockade. Together, these findings identify hSERT as a previously unrecognized molecular target of rosemary monoterpenes, suggesting that these compounds may act as partial inhibitors of serotonin transport. These results provide new molecular insights into the potential mechanism that may contribute to the reported neurobehavioral effects of rosemary, and support further investigation of these compounds in serotonergic signaling and neurotransmission.

articles.title: Neurotensin modulation of immune and oxido-inflammatory homeostasis targeting TGF-β activated kinase 1/Nuclear factor-kappa βeta pathway: an integrated in vivo and in silico study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Neurotensin (NTS) is a brain peptide and is known to regulate several brain pathways. Subsequently NTS involvement in psychosis was administered having its promising therapeutic effects as an antipsychotic drug. Therefore, it has been deduced that targeting the NTS system in the regulation of the immune organs would prove to be a productive strategy for developing the novel immune modulatory drugs. OBJECTIVE: The present study elucidated the potential anti-inflammatory properties of NTS receptor 1 (NTSR1) agonist PD149163 (PD) in modulation of immune organs specifically, spleen and thymus investigating the potential immunomodulatory mechanisms targeting NF-κB /TAK1 signaling pathway. METHODS: Swiss albino female mice were randomly grouped: Group I-control, treatment groups- Group II, Group III and Group IV were intraperitoneally exposed with NTSR1-agonist PD low dose/ PD50 (50 µg /kg bw), PD high dose/ PD100 (100 µg /kg bw) and NTSR1-antagonist SR48692 (500 µg /kg bw), respectively for 28 days. Biochemical, hematological, histopathological, and bioinformatics analyses were performed. Differences were considered statistically significant at P < 0.05. RESULTS: The levels of Nuclear factor kappa beta/NF-κB, Tumor necrosis factor- alpha/TNF-α, Interleukine-6/IL-6, Corticosterone/CORT and pro-oxidant, Lipid-peroxidation/LPx were visibly similar to control after the treatment of PD100 as well as PD50 dose however the elevation was observed with the SR. PD100 dose has a prominent effect on the plasma Interleukine-10/IL-10, CORT, NTS levels and tissue anti-oxidants superoxide dismutase/SOD, catalase/CAT as well as positively regulated the hematological and histological parameters, clearly deciphering NTS's immunomodulatory effects. Furthermore, in silico molecular docking analyses showed that PD exhibited high binding affinity with TGF-β activated kinase 1/TAK1 inflammatory protein, indicating inhibition of TAK1/NF-κB downstream signaling pathways. CONCLUSION: NTS receptor 1 analogs might provide a better understanding of the mechanisms by which NTS regulates immune-system and could be further exploited for managing various immune-related disorders.

articles.title: Preclinical Pharmacokinetic-Pharmacodynamic Modeling of Antibody Nanoconjugates for Breast Cancer Treatment.
articles.abstract: Over the past 5 years, the number of antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) entering the oncology market has surged. By contrast, the clinical use of immunoliposomes-nanoparticles that also employ antibodies as targeting agents (i.e., antibody-nanoconjugates, ANCs)-has yet to receive approval. One possible reason is the limited understanding of the relationship between ANC exposure and efficacy. To address this gap, we developed a pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) model for a docetaxel-trastuzumab ANC. PK and PD studies were conducted in MDA-MB-231 tumor-bearing mice, divided into three treatment groups: (i) control, (ii) free docetaxel + free trastuzumab, and (iii) docetaxel-trastuzumab ANCs. PK data were obtained by fluorescence imaging and captured systemic and tumor distribution of ANCs, while PD data were based on tumor growth measurements. The PK model was built using data from the ANC group, and the PD model was developed across all three treatment groups, with a leave-one-out cross validation strategy for predictive evaluation. Treatment schedule simulations were then performed. Using a population nonlinear mixed-effects (NLME) approach, the final PK model included a central and a tumor compartment, each with independent elimination rates. Tumor growth dynamics were best described by a reduced Gompertz model coupled with a Simeoni resistance model. This model demonstrated strong predictive performance. Using only data from the first two treatment cycles (4 time points) and Bayesian estimation in the test set, it accurately predicted systemic and tumor ANC concentrations across the subsequent four treatment cycles, with a relative error (RE) below 15%. Prediction precision was further improved (RE < 5%) when data from one additional treatment cycle were incorporated. Similar performance was achieved for PD data, with tumor volume predictions exhibiting RE < 15% and RE < 7.5% when implementing data from two and three treatment cycles, respectively. The model was then applied to simulate alternative treatment schedules. Interestingly, while systemic exposure remained comparable across regimens, every-5-day administration yielded the greatest tumor exposure compared to daily, weekly, and every-35-day dosing (mean ± SD tumor AUC: 55.4 ± 10.9 mg/kg day vs. 47.6 ± 9.38 mg/kg day, 51.4 ± 11.5 mg/kg day, and 44.6 ± 10.0 mg/kg day, respectively, one-way ANOVA, p < 0.001), highlighting the importance of dosing frequency. Overall, these results illustrate how PK/PD modeling can refine intra-tumor PK understanding and support preclinical development of innovative formulations such as ANCs.

articles.title: Retrospective Evaluation of the Association of Hypoalbuminemia With Acute Treatment Outcomes in Methicillin-Susceptible Staphylococcus Aureus Bacteremia.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cefazolin and antistaphylococcal penicillins (ASP) are first-line agents for methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA) bacteremia. These agents are substantially protein-bound; however, scant data exist evaluating the impact of hypoalbuminemia on microbiologic and patient outcomes for this indication. OBJECTIVE: The purpose of this study was to assess whether hypoalbuminemia is associated with delayed blood culture clearance in patients with MSSA bacteremia being treated with cefazolin or ASPs as definitive therapy. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included patients admitted for MSSA bacteremia between January 1, 2006 and December 31, 2019, with a serum albumin obtained between the date of an initial positive blood culture result and 72 hours following initiation of definitive therapy with cefazolin or an ASP. The primary outcome was the rate of persistently positive blood cultures, defined as failure to clear blood cultures within 72 hours of definitive therapy initiation. Patients with a serum albumin ≤2.5 g/dL were compared with those with an albumin >2.5 g/dL. Propensity score weighting was used to account for differences in cohort characteristics. RESULTS: A total of 123 patients were included. After propensity score weighting, patients with hypoalbuminemia had a higher rate of persistently positive blood cultures, both in the overall cohort (45.0% vs 13.2%, P < .001) and in the subgroups of cefazolin (33.0% vs 9.1%, P = .015) and ASP (60.1% vs 18.3%, P = .001) when analyzed separately. After propensity weighting in the combined cohort, the length of stay was longer in the hypoalbuminemic cohort, but no differences in mortality were observed. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Hypoalbuminemia was associated with a delayed 72-hour blood culture clearance in patients with MSSA bacteremia treated with either cefazolin or ASPs.
